newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi says working on treasury package.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi says working on treasury package.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in remarks published on Friday he was personally working on so-far unspecified treasury operations for 12.5 trillion lire contained in the government's 1997 budget.
"I would call them more financial operations more exactly," Ciampi told Il Sole 24 Ore in an interview. "I'm working on it myself, I'm working out solutions."
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's austerity 1997 budget, designed to slash next year's deficit by 62.5 trillion lire, is due to go before the lower house of parliament next week.
But Ciampi ruled out any budgetary "tricks". "I absolutely do not intend to do any," he told the newspaper.
"We're in touch with the European Commission. If there are any problems, I want to know about it first. I'm counting on arriving at 12.5 trillion in a completely transparent fashion."

He said: "I foresee measures which will be something more than financial operations. For some (measures), the effect will be prolonged without impacting either incomes, investment or consumption." He gave no details.
